title: Is This El Niño a 'Mega' One?
summary:
This year's El Niño keeps getting bigger nicknames. First people called it "Super El Niño." Then they called it "Godzilla El Niño." Now some people call it "Mega El Niño." But scientists say there is no new official name for it.

El Niño is a weather pattern. It happens when the water in the middle and east of the tropical Pacific Ocean gets warmer than usual.

A weather scientist named Ryan Maue put a map online. He said the sea near Peru and the Galapagos Islands was as much as 10 degrees Celsius warmer than normal. "This is now a Mega El Niño," he wrote.

But NOAA, the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, says something different. Its numbers show the sea is about 4 to 6 degrees Celsius warmer than normal in the eastern Pacific.

Emily Becker, a scientist at the University of Miami, said there is no need to invent a new group above "very strong." David Phillips, a weather expert in Canada, did not agree.
why_it_matters: Nicknames for weather can be fun, but the real numbers matter when you want to know what the weather will do.

background_read: El Niño is a weather pattern in the Pacific Ocean.
When the sea there gets warmer than usual, it changes the weather in many places around the world.
Scientists measure how warm the sea is and sort El Niño into groups, from weak to very strong.
